title: Finite monic tensor presentations and their evaluation maps
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and I a finite index type. For polynomials P_i in R[T], set C to the finite tensor product over R of R[T]/(P_i) [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If every P_i is monic, C has the basis indexed by tuples (e_i), 0 <= e_i < degree(P_i), consisting of tensor products of powers of the distinguished roots [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For any commutative R-algebra B and tuple x_i in B with P_i(x_i)=0, evaluation induces an R-algebra map C -> B sending each distinguished root to x_i. If the x_i generate B as an R-algebra, this map is surjective. Zero rings, empty I, and constant monic polynomials are allowed.

proof.text: Use the power basis of each AdjoinRoot(P_i), and apply Mathlib Basis.piTensorProduct. The tensor products of the component power bases give exactly the asserted finite basis.

Lift evaluation on each AdjoinRoot factor using P_i(x_i)=0. The product of these factor maps is multilinear, preserves the unit, and is multiplicative on pure tensors, so PiTensorProduct.liftAlgHom supplies the algebra map. Evaluate tensors with one nonunit factor to verify the distinguished-root equations.
The range of the evaluation algebra map contains every generator x_i. It therefore contains their algebraic span, which is B by assumption. Hence the map is surjective.

theorem presentationMap_surjective (P : ι → R[X]) (x : ι → S)
    (hx : ∀ i, aeval (x i) (P i) = 0)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range x) = ⊤) :
    Function.Surjective (presentationMap P x hx)
